old_caption: The video showcases a close-up view of a robotic mechanism, specifically focusing on a white, star-shaped robotic arm holding a textured, beige ball. The background is a solid blue, providing a stark contrast to the white and beige elements in the foreground. The robotic arm appears to be part of a larger machine, with visible wires and mechanical components extending from it. The ball, which has a rough, spiky texture, is securely held by the arm's fingers. Throughout the video, the ball is compressed and deformed by the robotic arm, and its segmented lines become more or less visible as it deforms, demonstrating the precision and control of the mechanism. The video captures the intricate details of the robotic components and the unique texture of the ball, emphasizing the advanced technology involved in such designs. There are no other objects or characters present in the scene, and the focus remains solely on the interaction between the robotic arm and the ball.

caption: The video showcases a close, fixed view of a beige spiky sphere resting inside a white three-petal star-shaped cradle. Metal servo housings appear at the left and right, and a bundle of multicolored wires lies at the lower left against a uniform blue background. The cradle, motors, wires, and framing stay in the same positions throughout, while the sphere turns in place. Small dark markers on the ball's surface shift toward the right side of the visible face and pass out of view. A seam or parting line becomes apparent across the sphere, and its apparent orientation changes as the surface pattern rotates. The spike grid tilts and slides relative to the fixed petals, showing continuous motion without any visible movement of the gripper itself within the view. The background and actuator positions remain constant, so the visible process is confined to the rotating spiky object held within the stationary cradle.

infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.
Aim for 85-115% of the original WISA word count,
and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
Return JSON {"caption":"complete revised caption",
"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
